cards.text: Ezekiel is a priest among the exiles by the River Kebar (Ezekiel 1:1-3), and the word of the LORD comes to him again. God calls him "son of man" and tells him to set his face against Mount Seir, where Esau, also called Edom, settled (Genesis 36:8). A prophet versus a MOUNTAIN, friend, and I already know who's got the bigger backup.
God doesn't warm up. No small talk, no "how's the weather on the mountain." First line out of the oven: "Behold, I am against you, O Mount Seir."

cards.question: God says He'll stretch out His hand against Mount Seir. What will He make it?
God says that when Mount Seir's cities are turned into ruins, Seir will know that He is the LORD.

cards.text: Now God gives the reason, and it goes way back. Mount Seir harbored an ancient hatred.

cards.question: Mount Seir harbored an ancient hatred. What did it do to the Israelites in the time of their disaster?

answers.text: Handed them over to the sword
Hid them in its mountain caves

cards.text: So God swears, "as surely as I live." Friend, when the One who made everything swears by His own life, you can set your oven timer by it.

cards.question: Mount Seir did not hate bloodshed. So God says bloodshed will ___ Seir.

cards.text: Mount Seir becomes a desolate waste, with nobody coming and going. Its hills, valleys and ravines fill with those killed by the sword.

cards.question: God says Mount Seir will be desolate for a while, and then its cities will be lived in again.

cards.text: Then God gives a second reason. Seir looked at two nations and countries and said, "These two nations and countries will be ours, and we will possess them"

cards.question: Mount Seir said those two nations and countries would be its own. But God points out a problem. What is it?

cards.text: Friend, that's calling dibs on the couch while the owner is sitting ON the couch. So God swears by His life again: He'll treat Seir according to the anger and jealousy it showed in its hatred.
And God heard every contemptuous word Seir said about Israel's mountains, like "They are desolate; they are given to us to devour!" Seir thought the mic was off, and the mic was NOT off.

cards.question: Mount Seir kept running its mouth about Israel's mountains. Who does God say Seir was really boasting against?

cards.text: Then God says that while the whole earth rejoices, He will make Seir desolate.

cards.question: God tells Mount Seir, "As you ___ when the inheritance of the house of Israel became desolate, so will I do to you."
God's word against Mount Seir reaches past one mountain: all of Edom will become a desolation too.

cards.text: Same prophet, new mountains. God tells Ezekiel to prophesy to the mountains of Israel. The enemy had said of them, "Aha! The ancient heights have become our possession" and God has something to say about that.

cards.question: God says the nations made Israel's mountains desolate, trampled them on every side and slandered them.

cards.text: So God speaks to every corner of the land, its hills, ravines, ruins and abandoned cities, all made a spoil and a mockery to the nations around. In His burning zeal, He has spoken against those nations and against all Edom.

cards.question: God says Edom took His land as its own possession with wholehearted ___ and utter contempt.

cards.text: God says He has spoken in His burning zeal because Israel's mountains have endured the reproach of the nations. Then He swears with an uplifted hand, like raising your right hand in court, only this time the Judge is the One making the promise.

cards.question: What does God swear will happen to the nations around Israel's mountains?

answers.text: They will endure reproach of their own
They will rule over the mountains forever
They will be left completely untouched

cards.text: And now the whole message turns on one little word: "But you, O mountains of Israel" Friend, after all those ruins, I can FEEL the oven warming up.

cards.question: God turns to the mountains of Israel with good news. What will those mountains do?
God says the mountains will bear fruit for His people Israel, because they will soon come home.

cards.text: To Mount Seir, God said, "Behold, I am against you" (Ezekiel 35:3). To the mountains of Israel, same "behold," COMPLETELY different news: "For behold, I am on your side"

cards.question: God says He will turn toward the mountains of Israel. What will happen to the land?

answers.text: It will be tilled and sown
It will be fenced and guarded
It will be left to rest

cards.text: And God will multiply the people on those mountains, the house of Israel in its entirety. Not a few stragglers, friend. EVERYBODY.

cards.question: God says the cities of Israel will be inhabited and the ruins ___.
God promises to make Israel's mountains as inhabited as they once were. What else does He promise?

answers.text: To make them prosper more than before
To let them prosper for a season
To keep them small and quiet

cards.text: Back to how it was AND then some, like getting your old job back with a RAISE. God will cause His people Israel to walk on these mountains and possess them as their inheritance.
But people had been saying of this land, "You devour men and deprive your nation of its children"

cards.question: Because of what people said, God declares the land will go on devouring men.
God makes one more promise to the mountains of Israel. What will He no longer allow to be heard against them?

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 7 quotes "as surely as I live.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 17 quotes "As you ___ when the inheritance of the house of Israel became desolate, so will I do to you.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "God doesn't warm up.", "No small talk, no 'how's the weather on the mountain.'" and "First line out of the oven: ...". Only the walkthrough's opening card may go up to 3.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke's core action is a promise that is certain because God swears by His own life. "Set your oven timer by it" plays on "set your watch by it," which means something happens on a regular schedule. That is a different action from a certain promise.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card tells Seir's judgment as something happening now ("Mount Seir becomes a desolate waste... Its hills, valleys and ravines fill..."). The text gives it as God's declaration of what He will do ("I will make Mount Seir a desolate waste... I will fill its mountains with the slain"). In a prophetic passage, this can read as narrated history.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "Seir thought the mic was off" states what Seir believed as a fact. The text never says what Seir thought, and the line isn't marked as Papa Dorin's guess.

rule.text: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: The story card right before card 17 says "while the whole earth rejoices." Card 17 then asks "As you ___ when the inheritance of the house of Israel became desolate," and the right answer is "rejoiced." The setup puts the answer word on screen just before the question.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences ("Same prophet, new mountains.", "God tells Ezekiel..." and "The enemy had said of them..."). It opens stop 2, but it isn't the walkthrough's opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question says "God turns to the mountains of Israel with good news." That rules out both wrong answers, "Stay bare as a warning" and "Become pasture for Edom," because both are bad news. Card 7's "I can FEEL the oven warming up" points the same way.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "And God will multiply the people...", "Not a few stragglers, friend." and "EVERYBODY."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
